People in India are switching to UPI because paying now takes a few seconds, costs nothing for most people, and works almost everywhere, from big stores to a roadside chai stall.

Three reasons stand out:

Speed and ease: Scan a code, type the amount, enter your PIN, done. The money moves in seconds, at any hour, even on holidays.
One system for every bank: You can use any UPI app with almost any bank account. Paying a friend, splitting a bill or paying a shopkeeper all work the same way, with no card or cash needed.
Very low cost: It is free for most everyday payments. Small shops don't need a card machine, only a printed QR code, so even tiny sellers can accept digital money.

Cheaper smartphones and mobile data helped it spread fast. It also feels safer than many options, since you never hand over card details. Your money goes straight from your bank to the other person's. Once a few shops and friends started using it, everyone else followed, because it was simply easier than carrying cash or waiting for change.
